title: BoneView at Poitiers University Hospital emergency department: fracture-detection AI is followed by fewer reading discrepancies and shorter stays
summary: At Poitiers University Hospital's emergency department, the X-ray discrepancy rate fell by 17% and mean stay by 9 minutes after Gleamer BoneView arrived (3,720 patients).
account: Radiologists and emergency physicians at Poitiers University Hospital, a level I trauma center in France, compared two six-month periods in their emergency department. From 1 January 2021 to 30 June 2021, clinicians had Gleamer BoneView, a commercial AI tool that marks likely limb fractures on radiographs; from 1 January 2020 to 30 June 2020 they did not. Among 3,720 trauma patients aged 17 or older, the rate of discrepancies between emergency physicians' and radiologists' readings fell by 17%, and mean length of stay in the department fell by 9 minutes. Clinically relevant discrepancies did not change significantly, and expert consultation fell by 1%, also not significant. The study is a retrospective before-and-after comparison at one hospital, and the authors declare no conflicts of interest.
purpose: BoneView was built to help clinicians detect fractures on radiographs. Fewer reading discrepancies were that purpose; the shorter stay was a related workflow gain.
location: Emergency department, Poitiers University Hospital, Poitiers, France
